item.title: Baker Mayfield returned to practice on Thursday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield appears to be trending toward playing on Sunday against the Lions.
item.content:encoded:
Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield appears to be trending toward playing on Sunday against the Lions.

After missing Wednesday's practice, Mayfield was back on the field for Thursday's session, according to multiple reporters on the scene.

Mayfield is dealing with foot and right thumb injuries, though the foot issue is what would keep him from playing.

But the fact that Mayfield is practicing on Thursday is a positive sign for his potential availability.

If needed, rookie Jalon Daniels would make his fourth start of the season on Sunday against Detroit.

Mayfield has completed 60.6 percent of his passes for 922 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions so far in 2026. He’s started six games.

Tampa Bay’s injury report with participation levels is set to be released later on Thursday.

item.title: Frank Reich: I'm the Jets' offensive coordinator, our inability to score starts with me
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Jets haven't scored a touchdown since the third quarter of their Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets haven't scored a touchdown since the third quarter of their Week 8 loss to the Raiders. It's now Week 11, and Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich knows it's past time for him to find a way to get his team into the end zone.

Reich said today that he believes the Jets have enough talent on offense to produce, and he and the coaching staff need to make it happen.

"I'm the offensive coordinator, it starts with me," Reich said. "I, and we as a staff, have to put the players in position to do what they do. We've got a very talented group, so we need to do a better job coaching."

Over the last nine quarters of play, the Jets have nine Jason Sanders field goals, and no other points. Reich is well aware that three points a quarter isn't going to win many games.

"Obviously, players need to do their part and execute and make plays," Reich said. "For all of us, it's a collective effort. We know we need to put more points on the board, whether it's in the red zone or whether it's further out, we still want to be explosive. We need to get back on track there. It's been nine quarters. Believe me, I feel every play of that nine quarters."

item.title: Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft advance to final round of Hall of Fame voting
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Belichick and Kraft were also finalists in last year's selection process.
item.content:encoded:
Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft will have another chance at election to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2027.

The Hall announced on Thursday that Belichick has been chosen as the nominee in the coach category while Kraft is the nominee in the contributor category. That was also the case last year, but neither of them were elected.

Belichick's failure to get enough votes for election created a particular outcry given the six Super Bowl titles he won while coaching Kraft's Patriots from 2000-2023.

The Hall of Fame overhauled selection procedures in the wake of last year's election. The size of the selection committee was cut in half from 50 to 25 and there is no longer be a separate category for senior players.

Belichick and Kraft will join 13 player nominees for consideration by the committee. That list of candidates will be reduced to seven before a final vote with 80 percent approval needed for election.

item.title: Ravens send CB Marlon Humphrey home, will not play him this week due to comments about Baltimore
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Head coach Jesse Minter said Humphrey will not be with the team for the rest of this week.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will not be in the lineup for the team's game against the Panthers on Sunday.

Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Thursday that Humphrey has been sent home for the rest of the week after saying the city of Baltimore is "best at making criminals" on the most recent episode of his podcast. Humphrey apologized for the comments on Wednesday, but Minter said the team determined this was the best choice for the organization.

"Internal conversations obviously with myself and the leadership of the organization, we’ve decided to deactivate Marlon for this game, this upcoming week," Minter said. "I know there’s gonna be a lot of questions. I said this yesterday, these conversations are very personal and private. To me, [they] need to remain that for the good of the team."

Minter was asked if Humphrey will have to do anything else in order to return to the lineup for their game against the Texans in Week 12. He said that was one of the conversations that will remain in house as the Ravens move forward.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer: Christian Parker still has a bright future with the Cowboys
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys' defensive play-caller on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys' defensive play-caller on Sunday. He replaces defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who will retain his title.

"Christian Parker is a huge part of what we're trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator," Schottenheimer said Wednesday, via Todd Archer of ESPN. "He is our leader. He is not changing any of those things, but I do feel that in the best interest of winning that Pet's calling the game is going to help us get to where we want to get to."

Schottenheimer said Parker would continue running meetings and leading walkthroughs, but the Cowboys needed "a different perspective" on game day.

Parker, 34, arrived in January as a first-time play caller, leaving Philadelphia after two seasons as the Eagles' defensive passing game coordinator. The Cowboys, though, rank last in yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8 percent). They are 30th in scoring (28.2).

Pettine arrived before Week 5 as a senior defensive assistant to help Parker, whom he brought into the NFL with the Packers in 2019. He was defensive coordinator with the Jets, when Schottenheimer was on staff, and also served in that role with the Bills and Packers.

Pettine was head coach of the Browns from 2014-15.

"When I look at this situation, we're all committed to trying to get it right," Schottenheimer said, "and so we're making adjustments like we've made. We've made adjustments. We've adjusted some scheme. We've adjusted some personnel. We've adjusted some play time. This is just another adjustment where we're trying to get right."

Schottenheimer made clear several times that he still believes in Parker and still believes Parker has a future with the Cowboys.

"CP has a very, very bright future as a coach, but more specifically, a very bright future here as our defense coordinator," Schottenheimer said.

item.title: Report: Mike Pettine takes over as Cowboys' defensive play-caller
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator.
item.content:encoded:
This one was inevitable, perhaps from the moment Mike Pettine arrived last month as an assistant.

Via ESPN, Pettine will be taking over as the play-caller for the Dallas Cowboys defense.

Pettine supplants defensive coordinator Christian Parker, a Pettine protege who is in his first year as the coach in charge of an NFL defense. Parker will remain the team's defensive coordinator.

It was obvious that something was coming. Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers included an embarrassing performance from the defense, highlighted by multiple players running the wrong way when receiver Deebo Samuel rumbled 70 yards for a rushing touchdown.

Some would say Pettine is part of the problem, given that he has been there for multiple weeks. Short of firing everyone and hiring someone off the street, however, there's not much that can be done right now.

The first test comes on Sunday, when the Cowboys host the one-win Titans. Four days later, Dallas faces the two-win Eagles. If the Cowboys don't win both, they'll likely be de facto done for 2026.

item.title: Deshaun Watson on future with Browns: That's up to my agent, I don't worry about that
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After several years marred by poor play and injuries, Deshaun Watson has provided some return on the investment the Browns made with the infamous 2022 trade to acquire him.
item.content:encoded:
After several years marred by poor play and injuries, Deshaun Watson has provided some return on the investment the Browns made with the infamous 2022 trade to acquire him.

Watson has engineered a league-high six game-winning drives for the Browns, who stand at 6-4 and the AFC’s current No. 7 seed.

The five-year commitment the franchise made to him is just about at its end, with 2026 representing the final season of the original deal.

With the team on its bye in Week 11, has Watson thought about an appropriate time to speak with the organization about his future?

“That’s up to my agent. So, that’s all David Mulugheta,” Watson said, via transcript from the team. “I don’t even worry about that, even all the way up to the last game. My future and what that holds is all in God’s hands, and whoever contacts David. Right now, again, it’s just playing good football, winning games, enjoying this moment, because it can all be taken away regardless. Right now, I’m just focusing on today, this bye week, and then getting back up here and finishing out the season strong for us.”

Asked as a follow-up if he’s opened the door for his agent to speak with the Browns about the future, Watson again sidestepped.

“Yeah, that’s a David question,” Watson said. “That’s my agent, I’m going to leave that up to my agent for sure.”

While the Browns have gone 6-3 with Watson as a starter so far in 2026, the quarterback’s numbers are not overwhelming. He’s completed 65.1 percent of his passes for 2,118 yards with seven touchdowns and four interceptions — good for an 89.1 passer rating. He’s also taken a league-high 37 sacks.

item.title: PFT's Week 11 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A wild guess for all 13 upcoming games.
item.content:encoded:
The heater is over.

After going 27-2 between Week 8 and Week 9, I regressed to the mean with a 9-5 week. It was inevitable.

This week, with six teams on byes, there are only 13 games. Which means that, at most, I'll get 13 of them wrong.

For the year, the record is now 96-53-1. That's a success rate of 64 percent.

Here goes nothing. Perhaps literally.

Colts at Texans (Thursday night)

At 3-6, time is running out for the Texans. If they can't beat the Colts at home, the Texans have no shot at pulling themselves back into the race for a wild-card berth.

Texans 23, Colts 16.

Dolphins at Bills

Buffalo has a rough stretch coming. This is the worst time to step into a trap. Fortunately, the Dolphins may not be talented enough to take advantage of the opportunity to catch the Bills napping.

Bills 30, Dolphins 13.

Ravens at Panthers

It's desperation time for Baltimore. If they can't win this one, they have little or no chance of closing the gap with the Browns for the No. 7 seed.

Ravens 20, Panthers 17.

Saints at Bears

It's a big week for the Bears, who can't afford to look past the Saints as Chicago prepares for a Thanksgiving showdown in Detroit.

Bears 27, Saints 20.

Titans at Cowboys

Tony Pollard's return to Dallas will give the Tennessee offense a lift, and the Titans generally have played better than the Cowboys in recent weeks.

Titans 30, Cowboys 27.

Buccaneers at Lions

It's a trap for the Lions, and they know it's a trap. While the game could leave them a little bruised and battered for the Thanksgiving visit from the Bears, the Lions will do whatever they have to do to get to 8-2.

Lions 24, Buccaneers 17.

Cardinals at Chiefs

They're getting the Cardinals at the perfect time. Then again, pretty much any time anyone gets the Cardinals is the perfect time.

Chiefs 34, Cardinals 10.

Steelers at Eagles

Pittsburgh has no chance at holding its ticket to another quick exit from the playoffs if it can't win the games it's supposed to win.

Steelers 16, Eagles 12.

Jets at Chargers

The Chargers have a chance to get on a little bit of a winning streak against a team that can't figure out how to get off a losing streak.

Chargers 24, Jets 21.

Raiders at Broncos

Fernando Mendoza's three-week "Welcome to the NFL" continues.

Broncos 27, Raiders 16.

Jaguars at Giants

Another week, another opportunity for Jacksonville to convince more people that they are elite.

Jaguars 30, Giants 20.

Vikings vs. 49ers (Sunday night; Mexico City)

Brian Flores will hold the San Francisco offense sufficiently in check for Kirk Cousins to outscore the San Francisco defense.

Vikings 24, 49ers 20.

Bengals at Commanders (Monday night)

Joe Burrow keeps thriving in standalone games.

Bengals 30, Commanders 21.

item.title: Mike LaFleur: I don't buy narrative that you can't evaluate Carson Beck in current offense
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cardinals are set to start Carson Beck at quarterback for the rest of the season and the rookie's performance over the remaining seven games will play a role in how the team approaches the offseason.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinals are set to start Carson Beck at quarterback for the rest of the season and the rookie's performance over the remaining seven games will play a role in how the team approaches the offseason.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur was asked if that evaluation will be compromised by the fact that injuries have taken players like wide receiver Michael Wilson, left tackle Paris Johnson, and running back Jeremiyah Love out of the lineup as Beck begins his time in the NFL. LaFleur said that he will be looking at what Beck does rather than at what's missing.

"I don't buy into the narrative that you can't evaluate," LaFleur said, via the team's website. "You can absolutely evaluate an individual guy. You can't always go off the production . . . but with his first start, he did everything we asked him to do."

Beck was 11-of-18 for 108 yards and two interceptions, so a lack of focus on production would seem to be a good thing for him when it comes to the evaluation process. At some point, that will have to play a role in how the Cardinals consider their options at the position in 2027, but LaFleur's eye is on other things for the time being.

item.title: Bears-Lions Thanksgiving audience will be huge — and it could have been even bigger
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last year, both of the early Thanksgiving Day games broke the prior record for NFL regular-season audience size.
item.content:encoded:
Last year, both of the early Thanksgiving Day games broke the prior record for NFL regular-season audience size. This year, the all-time record of 57.2 million from the Chiefs-Cowboys game is likely safe.

With one small tweak to the schedule, it perhaps wouldn't be.

In 2025, Packers-Lions attracted an incredible 47.7 million viewers. This year, the looming battle between the 7-2 Bears and 7-2 Lions should approach (if not match . . . if not beat) that number.

The problem is the second game. The 2-7 Eagles are in soft-tank mode. The 4-6 Cowboys have disintegrated into defensive disarray. While it will still attract a very large audience given the captive audience and the usual Thanksgiving routines, it likely won't approach 50 million.

While the NFL has granted a permanent hammerlock to the Lions and Cowboys for the traditional Thanksgiving afternoon games, a simple tweak would have set the stage for Bears-Lions to break 50 million — and perhaps to threaten last year's record.

Here's the idea. Why not install flexibility to flip the start times of the afternoon games?

It's no different than the usual Sunday-afternoon flex, like the one that happened this weekend when Steelers-Eagles moved from 4:25 p.m. ET to 1:00 p.m. ET and Jaguars-Giants slid to the higher-profile slot.

On Thanksgiving, the late-afternoon game always does better than the early one. In some years, the Lions game could be viewed as more attractive than the Cowboys game. This year would be one of those years.

It's something to consider. Getting an annual Thanksgiving Day game doesn't mean owning the window. And given the NFL's current willingness, on and after Week 12, to flex from Sunday to Thursday or Sunday to Monday, why not reserve the right to acknowledge that, for the two afternoon games on Thanksgiving, the "best" one should be played in the higher-profile slot?

item.title: 49ers WR Christian Kirk had meniscus surgery
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: 49ers wide receiver Christian Kirk went on injured reserve because of a knee injury a couple of weeks ago and that injury has also led him to the operating room.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Christian Kirk went on injured reserve because of a knee injury a couple of weeks ago and that injury has also led him to the operating room.

Kirk shared a picture of his knee post-surgery on Instagram on Wednesday night. The picture was part of a post commemorating Kirk's 30th birthday and he called this season, which began with another stint on injured reserve due to a calf injury, "the hardest of my career."

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Kirk had surgery on his meniscus. Neither he nor Kirk outlined any recovery timeline, but it seems like a long shot that he'll be returning to action this season.

Kirk only played in one game for the 49ers between the two injuries. He signed a one-year deal with the team this offseason, so he'll be a free agent come March if he does not re-sign with the team ahead of the 2027 league year.

item.title: Joe Burrow can become the first QB ever with 4+ touchdowns in 6 consecutive games
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Burrow and Peyton Manning are the only QBs ever with 4 TDs in 5 straight games. If Burrow does it again on Monday night, he'll be the first in NFL history to do it in 6 straight games.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is on a remarkable streak of four-touchdown games. If he does it again on Monday night, he'll do something no player in NFL history has done before.

Burrow has at least four touchdowns (combined running and passing) in each of the last five games. A four-touchdown game against the Commanders on Monday night would give Burrow an all-time NFL record six straight four-touchdown games.

Currently, Burrow and Peyton Manning are tied for the record, with five consecutive four-touchdown games. Manning did it in 2004 with the Colts. Burrow's last five games have featured:

Four touchdown passes in a 38-18 win over the Steelers.

Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons.

Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans.

Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens.

Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins.

Burrow is the MVP favorite, and with 2,795 yards and 27 touchdown passes through nine games this season, he's closing in on 3,000 yards and 30 touchdowns, which only four quarterbacks have done within their first 10 games of a season: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Manning in 2013 and 2014, and Patrick Mahomes in 2018. That's good company for a quarterback to be in, and Burrow is playing right now at a level few quarterbacks have ever reached.

item.title: Todd Monken: Getting flexed into Sunday night is really cool for our players
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism.
item.content:encoded:
If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism.

But with the way the season has unfolded, that's exactly what's happened.

With the Browns at 6-4 and the Raiders at 4-6 — and now starting the league's No. 1 overall pick at quarterback — the two clubs make for one of the most compelling matchups of Thanksgiving weekend that wasn't already in a standalone window.

Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Wednesday that getting flexed is “really cool for our players.”

“I said it at the beginning of the year. I mean, you want to be on Thursday Night, Sunday Night, Monday Night — you want to be flexed, means you’re having a good year,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “As nice as it is to have a one o’clock schedule every week, I mean, I said that, early in the [year]. I mean, you’re on a trajectory to be fired at some point because you’re at one o’clock every week. So, you’re fighting like hell to get to where you’re on national TV. So, if people are going to watch football, and more importantly than that, an opportunity to get to seven [wins].”

Monken also agreed that it’s a good test for the Browns as a young team.

“I think you earn where you’re at in the present moment, and that only lends itself to what’s in front of you and how important that’s going to become,” Monken said. “You know, getting the bye at 6-4 and putting yourself in position where the rest of the games matter, and especially the one coming up.”

This will be the Browns’ first Sunday night game at home since 2019, which should make for a rowdy atmosphere on the shores of Lake Erie.

“Oh, it’s a huge advantage. Huge advantage,” Monken said of the anticipated environment. “Making it hard for the opposing offense, cadence-wise, being able to function, and making an advantage for us when we’re on offense. I mean, it’s a huge advantage, and it should be playing at home.”

item.title: Jared Goff: Jahmyr Gibbs is a special player, special guy, special teammate
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Back in August, the Lions signed Jahmyr Gibbs to a three-year contract extension.
item.content:encoded:
Back in August, the Lions signed Jahmyr Gibbs to a three-year contract extension.

Gibbs has been paying it off.

The 24-year-old running back currently leads the league in rushing yards (1,000), rushing touchdowns (11), yards from scrimmage (1,384), and total touchdowns (13).

In his Wednesday press conference, quarterback Jared Goff praised Gibbs for his outstanding performance so far in 2026.

“You look at the numbers he's doing, it's like you hear his name mentioned with [Hall of Famer] LaDainian Tomlinson it seems like every week. And obviously we know about that guy and yeah, he's unbelievable,” Goff said, via transcript from the team. "He really is. He's a special player. He's a special guy, special teammate. The work he puts in I think gets unnoticed sometimes. He's a worker and has elevated his game from last year to this year in a lot of ways that you guys have obviously seen and it's paid off. It's been great for him and he's playing really well.”

Goff added that there’s plenty the public doesn’t see when it comes to Gibbs’ competitiveness.

“He's very competitive,” Goff said. “Anytime there's a competitive situation in practice, he wants the ball, he wants to make someone look silly, he wants to make somebody miss and he wants to make the play. And when he doesn't, he gets upset and that's kind of what you like to see when he makes a mistake or misses a block. He's truly upset about it and that's a sign of a good player and a guy who's striving for greatness.”

It’s also worth noting that Gibbs leads the league in rushing attempts (199) and touches (240). His previous career high in touches came last year with 320, which he appears poised to blow through.

item.title: Ben Johnson sees Bears' 4.2 yards per carry average as "a deceiving statistic"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt.
item.content:encoded:
League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt. The Bears also average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt. Bears coach Ben Johnson doesn't much care about that.

What Johnson does care about is that the running game is efficient, and Johnson would like to see better efficiency than he has seen so far from his offense. Johnson noted that an occasional long run can skew the yards per carry average, and if there are too many runs getting stuffed for no gain, that's a problem. On the flip side, a one-yard run will bring down any team's average, but it's a great play if it happens on fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line.

"I don't see it as bigger chunk runs, necessarily. The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways," Johnson said. "We run the ball a lot in the red zone, and when you're down there a four-yard carry is really an explosive."

Johnson said what he cares more about is efficiency. Many teams look at running success rate, which means the percentage of runs on which a team gains at least 40 percent of yardage needed on first down, at least 60 percent on second down, or at least 100 percent on third or fourth down. The Bears' success rate this season is 49.2 percent, and Johnson says that's not good enough.

"We go off efficiency, and we're under 50 percent efficient running the ball. We set our bar higher than that. We want to be closer to 55 percent, so we've got some work to do and all our guys know it," Johnson said.

Ultimately, Johnson wants to see rushing first downs and rushing touchdowns. Yards per carry is secondary to that.

item.title: Myles Price, NFL's top punt returner, shows he can make an impact on Vikings' offense, too
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Vikings have a big weapon on special teams in return man Myles Price, who is leading the league in punt return average, total yards and touchdowns, and is third in the league in both kickoff return average and total yards.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings have a big weapon on special teams in return man Myles Price, who is leading the league in punt return average, total yards and touchdowns, and is third in the league in both kickoff return average and total yards. But on Sunday against the Packers, Price showed that he can make an impact on offense, too.

In the Vikings' win over the Packers, Price got a career-high 33 snaps on offense, and he responded by catching four passes, including the first touchdown of the game on a 38-yard pass from Kirk Cousins. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen that the decision to give Price so much playing time was mostly because of injuries to starting receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings, but with the way Price performed, he'll get more playing time on offense going forward.

"We want to continue to find ways to get Myles involved in the offense," O'Connell said.

O'Connell said that when the Vikings are as thin at wide receiver as they were on Sunday, there are concerns about getting anyone else injured, and he was worried about seeing Price take hits in the return game.

"With all the injuries the other day, we had no way of getting another player up," O'Connell said. "There was not another body to have, so we actually went into the game for the first time since I've been here with four receivers up. Every time Myles returned a ball, you felt like we could be out of 11 personnel altogether here on one play. He did get banged up a couple times, we tried to feature the bigger groupings, and luckily he was able to return."

Ultimately, O'Connell believes that when Price has the ball in his hands in the open field, he can make big plays whether on offense or special teams.

"Myles is a guy that we feel very strongly about making that last move, making that last man miss, and being able to score," O'Connell said.

Expect to see Price do more of that for the rest of the season.

item.title: Mexico City altitude will affect the kicking game on Sunday night
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Vikings and 49ers face off in Mexico City on Sunday night, they'll be playing at the highest elevation any NFL game is ever played at: Estadio Azteca's altitude is around 7,300 feet.
item.content:encoded:
When the Vikings and 49ers face off in Mexico City on Sunday night, they'll be playing at the highest elevation any NFL game is ever played at: Estadio Azteca's altitude is around 7,300 feet. And that could have an impact on the kicking game.

Kickers and physicists alike have agreed that high altitudes can easily add five yards or more to field goal range. The air is thinner at altitude, and in Mexico City the altitude makes the air about 20 percent less dense than at sea level. In Denver, which is about 2,000 feet lower than Mexico City, the air is about 15 percent less dense than at sea level, and Denver's Mile High Stadium is well known for the boost it gives to kickers.

Vikings kicker Will Reichard has a career-long field goal of 62 yards, and 49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro's career long is 59 yards. Both kickers made their career longs at sea level, and they both should feel confident if called upon to attempt a kick from at least a few yards beyond 60 yards in Sunday night.

Kickoff strategy may also be a factor at altitude. Only 16 percent of all kickoffs in the NFL this season have gone for touchbacks, as teams believe it's better to try to pin their opponents deep on their own end of the field than boot the ball into the end zone. In Mexico City, it may be hard for a kicker to avoid kicking the ball into the end zone — or kickers might be able to get a higher trajectory on their kicks and make it even easier to pin their opponents deep.

And punts will travel several yards farther, which could be especially exciting for Vikings return man Myles Price, the NFL’s top punt returner, who might be able to reach top speed before the coverage can get to him if 49ers punter Corliss Waitman outkicks his coverage.

There's a lot of talk before games at altitude about how teams should acclimate so their players don't get out of breath in the thinner air. But that's not the only part of the game that players will need to adjust to on Sunday night. The kicking game will be significantly impacted.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan on the Brian Flores defense: "It's not just a fad"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: 49ers coach says the Minnesota defense puts pressure on everyone involved.
item.content:encoded:
49ers coach Kyle Shanahan has never beaten a Brian Flores defense. Which might be the most impressive thing that can be said about the Brian Flores defense.

They meet again on Sunday night in Mexico City, when Shanahan's 49ers play the Vikings, whose defense is coordinated by Flores.

“He's more unique than all the other 31 guys," Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday regarding Flores. "He's the one guy who commits to this and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He's been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He's as good as it gets at that stuff.

"Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it's usually a matter of time. I think offensive coaches used to like to say that early on, but it's too many years of it and it’s too many games in this year that they're sound. They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play-caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure's really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian it's 70-straight plays of that.”

It's not easy to beat in part because it's almost impossible to simulate in practice. As Devin McCourty has said, you think you have a plan and then the game starts and everything changes.

It changes in part because Flores seems to be constantly self-scouting and adjusting, defying the films to create pressure in new ways.

The goal is to eliminate the offense's built-in advantage that comes from knowing what the play will be by creating confusion for the entire offense. Who's rushing? Who's dropping into coverage? Who do I block? If that guy doesn't rush, what do I do?

It makes for a compelling chess match, with the 49ers needing to find a way to get the Minnesota defense on its heels.

A strong running game is a must. Wearing down the defense physically is required. When inevitable passing situations arise, the quarterback needs to quickly find the open man (if there is one) and get the ball out before the walls close in.

Sometimes, they close quickly. The strategy results in plenty of guys getting a free run at the quarterback, forcing a deer-in-the-headlights response — right before impact.

item.title: Diego Pavia is the first pick in the UFL draft

item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Diego Pavia went unselected in the 2026 NFL draft. Seven months later, Pavia became the first pick in the UFL draft.

The Columbus Aviators made Pavia the top selection.

It's no surprise. He'll create buzz. He'll sell tickets.

At some point, he'll have to show that he can compete with a level of football that isn't all that far below NFL quality. Every year, plenty of UFL players play their way into NFL opportunities.

Pavia can, too. He'll get his chance. What he does from there is entirely up to him.

Despite finishing second in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting, no team picked Pavia in April. He initially was invited to participate in the Ravens' rookie minicamp before being added to the 90-man roster on a tryout basis.

Pavia participated in the offseason program. He was released not long before the start of training camp. He has had no NFL opportunities since then.

item.title: Cam Ward: Shift in offensive philosophy "what we all wanted"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said earlier this week that the Titans recently shifted their offensive philosophy to put more on quarterback Cam Ward's plate over the rest of the season.
item.content:encoded:
Titans head coach Robert Saleh said earlier this week that the Titans recently shifted their offensive philosophy to put more on quarterback Cam Ward's plate over the rest of the season.

Saleh said the move was made "to be fair to Cam" as the team assesses his standing as their quarterback of the future. The early returns have been promising.

Ward is 74-of-110 for 716 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions while also running 12 times for 85 yards. On Wednesday, Ward said "it's a lot more up-pace and what I like" while adding that he isn't the only member of the offense who has been pleased by the change.

"It's what we all wanted, though," Ward said, via the team's website. "Because we know what makes us go as an offense, and it is going to continue to do good things for us in the future."

The shift in style hasn't resulted in any wins yet, but continued growth from Ward is the likeliest path to the Titans improving on that front as well before the year is out.

item.title: John Harbaugh: The sacks are going to come for Abdul Carter
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants linebacker Abdul Carter scores well in a number of metrics that measure pass rush, but that hasn't shown up in the ones that's most obvious to those watching the game.
item.content:encoded:
Giants linebacker Abdul Carter scores well in a number of metrics that measure pass rush, but that hasn't shown up in the ones that's most obvious to those watching the game.

Carter has two sacks and eight quarterback hits in nine games this season and he has not had a sack in the team's last four games. Some of that is related to increased double teams coming his way in the wake of Brian Burns's season-ending torn ACL, but any explanation falls short for those who have been wanting to see Carter overwhelm offenses since he joined the Giants as the third overall pick in 2025.

On Wednesday, Giants head coach John Harbaugh said "we want sacks" when asked about Carter but that he's confident they'll start to come because of what he sees from Carter's tape.

"He's a disruptive guy. I promise you they're accounting for him," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "And the sacks are just going to come. You've got to go play football. I mean, you can have a bunch of sacks and really not be playing that good too. We've seen that before too. So he's that kind of player. He's a disruptive player. He's a game changer, game wrecker, and I think there's going to be a lot of game wrecks in his future."

The Giants face the Jaguars this weekend and that's the start of a tougher run of opponents than the ones they faced thus far. That makes it an ideal time for Carter's effort to translate to the kind of big plays that can swing games in their direction.

item.title: Sean Payton won't use Aidan Hutchinson injury as a teaching moment
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Lions coach Dan Campbell has made his position clear regarding player celebrations, in the aftermath of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
Lions coach Dan Campbell has made his position clear regarding player celebrations, in the aftermath of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending knee injury. Campbell will not tell his players to stop celebrating.

Broncos coach Sean Payton agrees with Campbell's position.

“I’m kind of with Dan," Payton told reporters. "I saw the final comments. We’re teachers and we’re constantly… But we’re going to walk out of the doors, and there’ve been a lot of celebrations. I’m kind of with Dan there where it’s unfortunate. Two good players got hurt on the same play, and I think that there are a lot of other things that I would put on tape on a Friday, Saturday that are [teaching moments]. That I wouldn’t put that on.”

For starters, any non-contact ACL tear quite possibly is the result of a partially torn knee ligament that was on the brink of fully tearing. If Hutchinson's ACL tear hadn't happened when he landed after jumping to celebrate a sack of quarterback Drake Maye, it could have happened on the next play. Or the next.

And it's impossible to expect players to not celebrate. A great play is the product of hours of work and effort and discipline, most of which happens away from the public eye. In the arena, with thousands cheering and millions watching on TV, how can the human beings inside the uniforms be expected not to display human emotion?

Injuries happen in football. The vast majority happen during a play. Some happen after a play. It's unreasonable to reduce it to none; the players shouldn't be expected to minimize or eliminate the happiness they experience when everything they've done privately culminates in a public moment of achievement.

item.title: Nick Bosa: I don't think I've played my best football
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa's only stats in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys were one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties in 34 snaps.
item.content:encoded:
49ers defensive end Nick Bosa's only stats in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys were one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties in 34 snaps. It was his fourth consecutive game without a sack, a first in his career.

"I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said Wednesday, via Nick Wagoner of ESPN. "But now I'm really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats. But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now, so that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats."

Bosa exited the injury report in Week 10. But he has worked his way back from the torn ACL in his right knee in Week 3 of the 2025 season and a calf injury in Week 3.

He has played catch up with new coordinator Raheem Morris' scheme.

"I think there's a learning curve and . . . a lot of guys haven't had many reps in the scheme so far," Bosa said. "I'm trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am."

Bosa's last double-digit sack season was 2023 when he had 10.5. He totaled nine sacks in 14 games in 2024 and two in three games in 2025, with none this season.

"I'm not going to make excuses because nobody really cares," Bosa said. "But I'm going to get better and I'm pretty confident in that physically and how I'm playing."
